In March 1889 a cyclone struck Apia harbour, where American, German and British warships were facing each other over Samoa. Six warships were sunk or driven ashore and many sailors died; only the British ship escaped to open sea.

The powers had been backing rival Samoan chiefs in a civil war, and the standoff threatened a wider clash between Germany and the United States.

The storm cooled tempers. A conference in Berlin that year set up shared rule over Samoa, and ten years later the Tripartite Convention divided the islands. The writer Robert Louis Stevenson described the disaster.
